Animated beamer slide from a ggplot

Source: R/ggtex.R
ggtex.Rd

Writes a multi-page PDF in which page 1 shows the static layers (and axes, legend, titles) and page *k + 1* adds the first *k* animation steps, and returns the beamer code that shows one page per overlay (with beamer's `\only` command). Every page is cut from the same rendered plot, so nothing moves between steps.

Usage

ggtex(
  p,
  file,
  animate = NULL,
  scope = c("layers", "all", "all_but_theme"),
  width = 5.5,
  height = 3,
  title = NULL,
  tex = NULL,
  standalone = FALSE,
  graphics_path = NULL,
  include_width = "\\linewidth",
  start = 1,
  device = NULL,
  categorical = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

p

A saved ggplot object.

file

Path of the PDF to write (e.g. `"figures/turnout.pdf"`). Required.

animate

Layers at which a new step starts. Layers before the first entry are always shown; the last entry also reveals all later layers. `animate = c(3, 4, 5)` shows layers 1-2, then adds 3, then 4, then 5 and everything after it. `NULL` (default) reveals every layer on its own. A negative number removes a step again: `-3` makes the step that started at layer 3 disappear (with the given `effect` as exit animation in PowerPoint), e.g. `animate = c(3, 4, 5, -3)`. Entries play in the order given, and `effect`, `trigger` and `duration` count removals as steps.

scope

What the numbers in `animate` count. `"layers"` (default): only geoms, stats and annotations; axes, titles, legend and theme are always shown. `"all"`: every `+` component of the plot in the order it was written (geoms, `labs()`, scales, coords, facets, `theme_*()`, `theme()`). `"all_but_theme"`: like `"all"`, but `theme()` and `theme_*()` calls are not counted and always applied. For these two, the plot must be made with [steps()], or its code written directly into the call.

width, height

Size of the PDF in inches. Use the size the plot will have on the slide so text sizes match (a full 16:9 beamer frame is about 5.5 x 3).

title

Frame title. `NULL` for no title.

tex

Optional path of a `.tex` file to write the code to.

standalone

If `TRUE`, the code is a complete, compilable beamer document instead of a single frame.

graphics_path

How `file` is referred to in the LaTeX code. Defaults to `file`, or to its path relative to `tex` if `tex` is given.

include_width

Width passed to `\includegraphics`.

start

First overlay number, if the frame has other overlays before the plot.

device

PDF device; `grDevices::cairo_pdf` (if available) handles Unicode and system fonts, `grDevices::pdf` is the fallback.

categorical

If `TRUE`, every group within a step (each bar, box, colour group, ...) gets its own overlay, in group order. See [ggppt()].

verbose

If `TRUE` (default), the LaTeX code is printed to the console.

Value

The LaTeX code (invisibly); it is also printed if `verbose = TRUE`.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey70") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  geom_point(data = subset(mtcars, mpg > 30), colour = "red")
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
ggtex(p, out, animate = c(2, 3), title = "Fuel use")
#> \begin{frame}{Fuel use}
#>   \centering
#>   % gganimslide: static 1 | 2 geom_smooth | 3 geom_point
#>   \only<1>{\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,page=1]{/tmp/RtmpIRxLoG/file190b6ff0bdd0.pdf}}%
#>   \only<2>{\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,page=2]{/tmp/RtmpIRxLoG/file190b6ff0bdd0.pdf}}%
#>   \only<3->{\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,page=3]{/tmp/RtmpIRxLoG/file190b6ff0bdd0.pdf}}%
#> \end{frame}
